children: Malaysia's export-oriented industries, particularly the electrical and electronics sectors, should continue to benefit from the ongoing global technology upcycle driven by digitalization and AI adoption, RHB senior economist Chin Yee Sian says in a note. Export momentum is expected to remain supported by resilient manufactured and commodity exports, while domestic demand and investment should provide an additional buffer for industrial activity. However, the external outlook remains exposed to a potential slowdown in AI investment, geopolitical tensions and U.S. tariff policies, she says. Prolonged tensions and elevated oil prices could raise business costs and weaken global demand, but Malaysia's diversified export base should provide some buffer against external headwinds. RHB expects further upside to its 2026 exports growth estimate of 21.7%, given year-to-date growth of 31.2%. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
